parts.note: reads like a businessman busy with commercial affairs, but the affairs are love affairs, pointing to the legendary Spanish seducer

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary libertine from Spanish literature is the archetype of a man who conducts endless romantic affairs.

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid, plain-speaking
an air is a look or appearance, as in 'an air of confidence'

explanation.surface: Someone blurts out a frank warning, shouting at a companion to look out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look out!' reads as a single warning, but it splits: 'Look' gives the second piece and 'out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the open air means being out of doors, outside rather than indoors.

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the word for the stone

parts.note: jet is a black stone used in jewellery
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl is carving an article out of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: He will try to cook rarebit

indicators.note: cooking the letters of rarebit mixes them into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef sets out to make Welsh rarebit, a cheese-on-toast dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' suggests attempting, but here it is the legal sense: someone who tries a case or dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or referee who hears and decides a dispute is someone who tries it.

parts.note: an essay is a piece of writing
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone attempted a letter to the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is an old literary verb for attempt, so its past tense is a synonym of tried.

clue.text: Gloomy with ulcer: a case for the doctor

indicators.note: the word for the ulcer forms a casing around the doctor's letters

parts.note: an ulcer is a sore
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient feels gloomy about an ulcer that needs a doctor to see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a case for the doctor' reads as a medical case needing attention; here 'a case for' means the sore encloses MB.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and melancholy, a close synonym of gloomy.

parts.note: reads like a select meeting of writers, but is a gathering of chosen pieces of writing collected in one book

explanation.definitionFit: A collection of selected poems or stories, from the Greek for a gathering of flowers.

clue.text: Right in, but it's taken out

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the other piece

parts.note: but and except both mean 'other than'

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is right to put something in, but it has been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken out of a longer work.

clue.text: Concert party in an arrangement of hues

indicators.note: the party's short name is placed inside the arrangement of hues

parts.note: coloration is the arrangement or pattern of colours
Lab is the short form of Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: A party at a concert is held in a room decorated in arranged colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is the noun of acting together, as in 'in concert', not a musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means working jointly with others, which is what this joint working is.

clue.text: Chopped and changed when solving this clue

indicators.note: the letters of the word when are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes chopping and changing their mind while solving the clue in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped and changed' is an idiom for vacillating; 'solving this clue' is a playful aside telling the solver to act on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn wood has been cut with an axe, so it has been chopped.

parts.note: reads as magic, but taken as witch's craft it means the vehicle a witch flies on

explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a witch flies on a besom, so it is literally the craft or vehicle of a witch.

clue.text: Father's bird is no longer in her prime!

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive S
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A father's girlfriend is mocked as being no longer young.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase describes someone too old to do what they once could, past their best.

clue.text: Pig in fat calls for old port

indicators.note: the pig is placed inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for pork cooked in fat, with a glass of old port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is the left side of a ship, whose older name this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The left-hand side of a ship was formerly called this before the word port replaced it.

parts.note: reads like advice to study science, but physics here is the old plural of physic, medicine, so a doctor orders a course of treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The clue's past-tense 'Recommended' sits against a present-tense answer: read it as the action a doctor takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who orders a course of medicine for a patient does exactly this.

clue.text: Become comfortably established in seat on row

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench seat with a high back
a din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: Someone settles comfortably into a seat in a row at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Having adjusted to a new home or job, one is comfortable and at ease there.

definitions.meaning: General William ... founded the Salvation Army
a small stall at a market or fair

explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small covered stand, and Booth was the first General of the Salvation Army.

clue.text: It's loud for a musical note

parts.note: taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician explains that a marking means loud for a particular note.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian marking means play loudly.

parts.note: food that has gone mouldy is off
a load is a cargo

explanation.surface: A ship's crew throws a rotten cargo overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload or get rid of something, as one jettisons unwanted goods.

clue.text: Serious measure needed for those that are late

parts.note: grave means serious
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Serious action is needed to deal with latecomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy, but means dead, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery is the place set aside for the dead, the late.

definitions.meaning: ... means large quantities, as in '... of water'
books, especially one of a set

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both large amounts and bound books.

clue.text: Sailor comes up a rope — this one?

definitions.text: Sailor comes up a rope — this one?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading the sailor's word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
a line is a rope on a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor climbs the rigging, and the clue asks which rope it is.
explanation.definitionFit: These small ropes fastened across the shrouds form the rungs sailors climb up the rigging.

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the fruit

parts.note: pears are fruit

explanation.surface: Stones have been left inside some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' suggests fruit pits, which the surface supports; it means gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems taken from oysters are counted among precious stones in jewellery.

clue.text: Members of this society have a lot in common

definitions.text: Members of this society have a lot in common

parts.words: Members of this society have a lot in common
parts.note: reads as people sharing interests, but 'a lot' is plenty of money, which all the wealthy share

explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy society is one whose members all have plenty of money.

definitions.meaning: a bird ... on a branch, settling there
animal lungs, traditionally fed to cats

explanation.definitionFit: To light is to alight or settle, and lights are offal lungs used as pet food.
The phrasal verb means both choose and assault.

parts.note: reads as a periodical for female readers, but a magazine is also a store for gunpowder, and the ladies' cloakroom has the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A powder magazine stores gunpowder; the same name is a polite term for a ladies' lavatory.

indicators.note: the article goes inside the wood

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lovely object is found in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old word for beautiful, as in 'fair maiden'.

definitions.meaning: the property of a number being not divisible by two

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both peculiarity of manner and the state of a number not being even.

parts.note: reads like an intruder walking into a workplace, but the office is a position of power seized without right

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes a throne or position of authority without a lawful claim.
